chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the skilled/tradesman who is trustworthy. And in another narration: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, loves the believing skilled/tradesman.'

key_terms.الْأَمِينَ: The trustworthy, honest, or reliable one
key_terms.الْمُحْتَرِفَ: The skilled person, tradesman, or one who has a profession/craft
key_terms.رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى: Another narration (indicating variant wording in the chain)

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about having a profession and being trustworthy?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on professions, this hadith links the Prophet’s and Imam’s teachings to emphasize that professional competence (ihtiraf) is a spiritual virtue when paired with trustworthiness or faith. In Shia tradition, this underscores the dignity of labor, affirming that earning a halal livelihood through skilled work is an act of worship that pleases Allah.
